applicable_when: The kernel is bottlenecked by two compounding problems rooted in the fixed tile configuration. (1) 128 registers/thread with BLOCK_M=64xBLOCK_N=64 tiles limits the SM to only 4 blocks (16 warps), yielding 6.25% occupancy — far too few warps to hide latency. (2) The shared memory access pattern for the B matrix (stride_bn=240, stride_bk=1 with non-power-of-2 leading dimension) causes ~12-way bank conflicts, consuming 77.5% of all shared load wavefronts as replays. The MIO scoreboard stall (64.6% of cycles) is a direct consequence. Reducing tile sizes (e.g., BLOCK_M=32, BLOCK_N=32) will cut register pressure, increase occupancy, and reduce the bank-conflict surface. Adding @triton.autotune with multiple configurations covering smaller tiles and varying num_warps/num_stages lets the runtime find the optimal point for this M=7840, N=40, K=240 problem shape on H200.
